chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Mu'adh ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Be patient with the enemies of the favours (of God), for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything better than obeying Allah regarding him.

key_terms.أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ: Enemies of the favours (those who are ungrateful or hostile to God's blessings)

ai.seo_question: What is the best way to respond to those who are ungrateful for God's blessings?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the pinnacle of patience (sabr) not merely as endurance, but as active obedience to God in the presence of those who disobey Him. This teaching, central to Shia ethical theology, transforms interpersonal conflict into a mechanism for spiritual elevation, emphasizing that one's reward is measured by the quality of one's worship amidst adversity. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining inner peace and divine favor when dealing with enemies or ungrateful individuals.
